head: f1037e38084c94e22e4bb0511cdbe524169a49eb
summary:
C-001 and C-003 no longer pin a settled count. Get-ExpectedSettled (tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1:209-233) counts the indent-2 items of the yaml's rules: list and subtracts $Twinned = 15. It never reads parity output. I re-measured every figure on the real tree:
- The yaml has 48 '  - name:' items, and Fitness op=check reports the same 48 rules, all holding. 48 - 15 = 33, which matches the settled count rules-parity prints under both shells (AGREE 11/15/27, 33 settled).
- C-001 and C-003, each run alone, exit 0 under both pwsh and powershell.exe as the outer shell (33 and 34).
- C-007 against the engine exits 0 under both outer shells.
- SettledCountProbe -Shape All exits 0 with all 9 shapes green.
- The full RuleCases -Case All exits 0 in 233 s, with 415 ok checks across C-001 to C-014.

I also ran my own mutations on scratch copies, separate from the probe:
- 3 entries appended under two markers: C-001 stays green at 36 under both outer shells.
- Parity printing settled-1: C-001 fails with 4 checks.
- Parity printing facts+1: C-001 fails with 4 checks.
- The pre-fix RuleCases.ps1 run against the current yaml: fails, expecting 28.

The guard regex hits the pre-fix file at exactly lines 205 and 268, and nothing in the current file.

The tree was clean afterwards and I removed my temp folders. There was one build attempt, so no loop. Deviations stand as recorded, in particular the oracle source changed per O-015. The guard rule's 'because' text still names the Fitness rule count as the source. It is not wrong (48 = 48), but it has drifted from the code, as code-review recorded. Contact is `code`: these are repo scripts and the engine's Fitness check, not a live environment.

checks.what: Parity tool on the real tree under both shells
checks.evidence: Both shells exit 0 and print 'rules-parity: AGREE 11 facts <- 15 twinned entries, 27 patterns; 33 settled entries not compared'.

checks.what: Independent count of yaml rule entries (not via parity or the oracle)
checks.command: ReadAllLines .taad/fitness.yaml; count '^  - name:' and group '^( *)-( |$)' by indent
checks.evidence: There is one column-0 key (rules: at line 71). It has 48 indent-2 items, all '- name:', plus 102 items at indent 4 and 48 at indent 6. 48 - 15 = 33 matches the parity tool.

checks.what: Engine Fitness check on the current tree (guard rule does not fire on fixed code; rule count equals yaml count)
checks.evidence: 48 rule(s) checked against 82 file(s) read, and every declared rule holds.

checks.what: C-001 and C-003 alone, with pwsh as the outer shell
checks.evidence: C-001: exit 0, 8 ok, expects 33 settled for both inner shells, with and without -ExpectFacts 11. C-003: exit 0, all ok, and the appended-entry check expects and sees 34.

checks.what: C-001 and C-003 alone, with Windows PowerShell 5.1 as the outer shell (oracle evaluated under 5.1)
checks.evidence: Same as under pwsh: C-001 exits 0 with 33, and C-003 exits 0 with 34.

checks.what: C-007 against the engine under both outer shells (oracle premise twinned + settled = Fitness rule count)
checks.evidence: pwsh: exit 0 in 24 s. powershell.exe: exit 0 in 23 s. Both print 'ok the Fitness rule count equals the yaml entries (twinned + settled)' and the clean scenario reads CLEAN.

checks.what: Full RuleCases suite with the engine (regression across C-001..C-014)

criteria.criterion: 1. C-001 asserts the parity summary line on the current tree (both shells, with and without -ExpectFacts 11), which already includes this slice's own settled entry
criteria.how: RuleCases -Case C-001 run alone exits 0 under pwsh and powershell.exe as the outer shell. It gives 8 ok checks, and the expected line has 33 settled (the survey had 32, and SL-053's own entry is included).

criteria.criterion: 2. C-001 stays green with one extra settled entry appended below the marker
criteria.how: The probe's AppendOne gives 34 under both shells. My own scratch copy with 3 extra entries gives 36 and exits 0 under both outer shells.

criteria.criterion: 3. C-001 stays green when one slice appends two settled entries under one marker
criteria.how: The probe's AppendTwo gives 35. My own copy had two entries under SL-900 plus one under SL-901: 36, exit 0.

criteria.criterion: 4. C-001 still fails when the parity tool prints the wrong count
criteria.how: The probe's CountPlusOne (settled+1) exits 1 with 4 failed. My own settled-1 mutation also exits 1 with 4 failed.

criteria.criterion: 5. C-001 still fails when parity is not AGREE with otherwise identical counts
criteria.how: The probe's NotAgree (DRIFT on the AGREE line) exits 1 with '4 check(s) failed.' under both shells. My facts+1 mutation also shows the rest of the line is still asserted exactly.

criteria.criterion: 6. C-001 does not let the oracle absorb a misclassification (14 twinned, settled+1)
criteria.how: The probe's Misclassified exits 1 with 4 failed under both shells. The oracle subtracts the pinned $Twinned and never uses the tool's figure (RuleCases.ps1:228).

criteria.criterion: 7. C-003 asserts the count after appending one entry, with the base taken from the unmodified tree
criteria.how: C-003 run alone exits 0 under both outer shells and expects 34 (33+1, computed before the append at :300). The probe's C003Base fails with 2 checks when the tool does not move or moves by two.

criteria.criterion: 8. The oracle fails by name when its source is unavailable, and C-001 works run alone
criteria.how: The probe's OracleUnavailable: with the yaml deleted, C-001 prints 'ExpectedSettled: fitness rule count unavailable' and exits 1, and C-002 on the same copy stays green. Lone -Case C-001 is green on the real tree. The 'interpreter missing' half no longer applies, because O-015 made the oracle a direct yaml count that needs no interpreter.

criteria.criterion: 9. The oracle works under both shells (scalar, single or array shapes)
criteria.how: C-001 and C-003 run with both powershell.exe and pwsh as the outer shell (both green). The probe's BothShells covers 33 settled entries and the single-entry yaml (1 settled) under both shells. The direct line count returns an [int], so the object-shape concern no longer applies.

criteria.criterion: 10. Oracle premise: C-007 (twinned + settled = Fitness rule count) on the current tree
criteria.how: C-007 exits 0 under both outer shells ('the Fitness rule count equals the yaml entries'). Fitness op=check reports 48 rules, and the direct yaml count is 48.

criteria.criterion: 11. The guard rule fires on the defect and not on correct code
criteria.how: Select-String with the rule's regex hits the pre-fix file (0647ead17) at exactly 205 and 268 and the current file nowhere. The engine's Fitness check passes on the current tree, and the probe's GuardRule agrees.

criteria.criterion: 12. The oracle guards against a non-positive derived count
criteria.how: The probe's OracleUnavailable with the yaml cut to only twinned entries (15 rules) prints 'ExpectedSettled: derived count 0 < 1' and exits 1 under both shells. Fewer than 15 was not run separately; the guard at :229 is `-lt 1`.

obligations.evidence:
The independent source exists and agrees:
- RuleCases -Case C-007 exits 0 under pwsh (24 s) and powershell.exe (23 s), with 'the Fitness rule count equals the yaml entries (twinned + settled)' ok.
- The engine's Fitness op=check reports 48 rules, the yaml has 48 '  - name:' items, and 48 - 15 = 33 matches rules-parity's settled count.
Per O-015 the shipped oracle is the direct yaml count, not Fitness's count, but the two are equal on this tree.

C-001, C-003 and C-007 were each run as a lone -Case under both powershell.exe and pwsh as the outer shell, and all six runs exit 0. The shipped oracle is the direct yaml count (O-015), and it evaluates under 5.1 and 7 alike.

SL-053's guard entry sits under '# settled by SL-053' at .taad/fitness.yaml:595. rules-parity under both shells prints '11 facts <- 15 twinned entries, 27 patterns; 33 settled', so facts, twinned and patterns are unchanged and settled went from 32 to 33.

not_reached: No engine gate runs tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1 or tests/rules/SettledCountProbe.ps1 (O-005 is still open). Whether C-001 stays green after the NEXT real engine append was simulated on scratch copies, not observed. The only real append observed is SL-053's own entry, and C-001 is green on it.
Adding a twinned entry (a new Fact) still requires a hand edit of $Twinned, 11 and 27 in RuleCases.ps1 and SettledCountProbe.ps1. That path was not exercised, by design.
SettledCountProbe was driven only from pwsh as the outer shell. Its own driver code under Windows PowerShell 5.1 was not run by me for the eight non-GuardRule shapes.
I judged the guard rule's firing on the pre-fix file with .NET Select-String using the same regex. I did not re-run the engine's Fitness against the pre-fix file; build-slice recorded that run.
C-007 and the full suite depend on machine-specific engine paths (%APPDATA%\taad3\venv, C:\Users\sshub\projets\taad_v3\backend at 020811e). Another machine or engine revision was not tried.
